question: Who became the first Indian chess player to be ranked No.1 in the live FIDE rankings in 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**R Praggnanandhaa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa** emerged as the top-ranked Indian player in the **Live FIDE Rankings** in **early 2025**, following a series of exceptional performances in elite international tournaments.
 
• In **January 2025**, during the **Tata Steel Chess Tournament** held in **Wijk aan Zee**, **Netherlands**, Praggnanandhaa gained critical rating points to leapfrog his compatriots in the live ratings list.
 
• By achieving this feat, he briefly surpassed the ratings of long-time **India No. 1** **Viswanathan Anand** and the high-flying **Arjun Erigaisi**.
 
• At the age of **19**, **Praggnanandhaa** became one of the youngest players in history to lead the Indian contingent in the **FIDE** live rating charts, which update after every single game played in rated tournaments.
 
• His rise to the top spot highlights the intense competition in **Indian Chess**, where multiple players are currently ranked within the **World Top 15**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Arjun Erigaisi:**
 
 
• **Arjun Erigaisi** is a **Grandmaster** from **Telangana** who became the **second Indian** after **Viswanathan Anand** to cross the **2800 ELO** rating mark in **2024**.
 
• He has been a consistent performer in the **French Top 12** and various **Open** tournaments, maintaining a spot in the **World Top 5** throughout late **2024** and **2025**.
 
 
 
• **D Gukesh (Dommaraju Gukesh):**
 
 
• **D Gukesh** created history in **December 2024** by defeating **Ding Liren** to become the **youngest-ever World Chess Champion**.
 
• Hailing from **Chennai**, **Tamil Nadu**, **Gukesh** won the **Candidates Tournament 2024** in **Toronto**, **Canada**, to earn his title shot.
 
 
 
• **Viswanathan Anand:**
 
 
• A **five-time World Chess Champion**, **Viswanathan Anand** became India's first **Grandmaster** in **1988**.
 
• Often referred to as the **"Tiger of Madras,"** he held the **India No. 1** position for over **three decades** before the emergence of the "Golden Generation" of Indian chess prodigies.
 
 
 
• **FIDE (International Chess Federation):**
 
 
• **FIDE** is the governing body of the sport of chess, headquartered in **Lausanne**, **Switzerland**.
 
• It maintains the official **ELO rating system** and organizes the **World Chess Championship** cycle. **Live Rankings** are unofficial real-time updates of these ratings between the publication of the official monthly lists.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Live vs. Official Ratings:** The **Live FIDE Ranking** is a real-time tracking of rating changes, whereas **FIDE** publishes the official rating list on the **1st of every month**.
 
• **Milestone Dates:** The year **2024** was a watershed year for Indian chess with the **45th Chess Olympiad** in **Budapest**, where both the **Indian Men’s** and **Women’s teams** won **Gold Medals** for the first time.
 
• **Grandmaster Title:** To become a **Grandmaster (GM)**, a player must achieve a **FIDE rating** of at least **2500** and earn **three GM norms** in international competition.
